newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent trims losses but holds in Friday's range.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent trims losses but holds in Friday's range.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures recovered from a lower opening to trade slightly higher at midday, but prices were trapped in Friday's range to underline the quiet tone after last week's volatility.

At 1134 GMT, July Brent, which lost three percent in value in the last week of May, was off three cents at $19.37 a barrel after edging up to a day's high of $19.43. June gas oil traded 50 cents lower at $172 a tonne.

Peter Gignoux, head of Smith Barney's petroleum desk in London, said prices have had a tendency to trade sideways in quiet activity and then make a sharp, quick move that draws in the speculative traders.
"We seem to drive down the road and a twister hits us and then, bang, it moves up a dollar or down a dollar, and then we go down the road again," he said.
"I suppose...the next twister on the horizon will be the OPEC meeting (on June 25)," he said, warning that crude prices may hover near $19 for the time being.
He said gasoline prices, which tend to be the market focus as the summer driving season kicks in, has not been the "locomotion" for the complex, removing another prop.

Traders said they were hoping for direction from NYMEX but no immediate impact was expected when the United Nations Secretary-General offers his recommendations to the Security Council on the renewal of the Iraq oil deal.
High-ranking U.N. officials said last week that Kofi Annan would certainly favour a six-month renewal of the $2 billion accord at current oil sales limits.
